run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T22:14:55Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: Observed facts: frontend ERROR span volume, which had been zero from about 21:52 to 22:14, rose sharply from ~22:14 and fell back to zero by 22:30, peaking at ~1797 error spans per 10-minute window at 22:21. Almost all of it is GET /api/data failing (≈393 error spans in 22:11–22:31) through the frontend client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (≈393, status 14 UNAVAILABLE); a smaller part is POST /api/checkout (≈43) failing through grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, whose exception text is a refused connection to payment's ClusterIP. The refused addresses in the spans are exactly the ad and payment Service ClusterIPs (ad 100.65.180.246:8080, payment 100.70.188.60:8080), and the failing ad trace contains no ad server span at all. At 22:13:21Z both the ad and payment Deployments were rolled (event trace: new ReplicaSets ad-6cb57f76d and payment-9c8ffb665 scaled 0→1 at 22:13:21, old pods killed at 22:13:24/22:13:25), and both Deployment pod templates carry kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T22:13:21Z with identical image (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad / -payment) and identical env. A hypothesis, not an observed fact: because the ad pod template declares no readiness/startup probe, the new pod was reported Ready at 22:13:24 while the ad process only logged "Ad service starting." at 22:17:48; the ad ClusterIP therefore routed to a pod that was not yet listening, producing the ECONNREFUSED errors until ad resumed serving requests (~22:18–22:19). ad's own server spans never carried an error status and payment logged successful charge transactions during the window, so the fault-injection settings adFailure=on and paymentFailure=100% that are currently in ConfigMap flagd-config do not match the observed error signature; they remain an unverified candidate. Who or what issued the rollout restart is not observable.

claims.text: frontend STATUS_CODE_ERROR span increase (10-minute window) was 0 from the sampled start of the window until about 22:14, then rose through 95.8/525.3/769.8/984.4/1226.3/1460.0/1619.9/1796.8 at 22:15–22:22, held at 1796.8 at 22:23, and declined to 0 by 22:30, while frontend STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans stayed around 26k–29k per 10 minutes.

In 22:11–22:31 the frontend ERROR span increases were dominated by GET /api/data (393.11), grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (393.11), GET (393.11) and executing api route (pages) /api/data (393.11), with a smaller POST /api/checkout (43.34), grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (43.34) and executing api route (pages) /api/checkout (43.34); frontend-proxy ingress measured 449.86 and router frontend egress 436.45 errors, checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge 34.83 each, and no ERROR series was returned for ad's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds.

Trace 39738559ae15135780326c17f7d13235 (spans starting ~22:14:27) shows load-generator GET failing with frontend GET and GET /api/data returning HTTP 500; the frontend span 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' carries exception.message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080 (2025-12-15T17:50:45.363Z)' and the client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds records rpc.grpc.status_code 14 / otel.status_code ERROR, while the trace contains no ad service span.

Service ad is ClusterIP 100.65.180.246 with port 8080/targetPort 8080 and selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad; Service payment is ClusterIP 100.70.188.60 with port 8080/targetPort 8080. The two addresses in the span error messages are therefore the Service ClusterIPs, and the current Endpoints map them to ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 (100.96.4.142) and payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 (100.96.4.221).

Trace f9632df3f1388a8011baad26248e0c46 shows frontend POST and POST /api/checkout returning 500, and the frontend CheckoutService/PlaceOrder client span (rpc.grpc.status_code 13) carries '13 INTERNAL: failed to charge card: could not charge the card: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused"'.

Kubernetes events in otel-demo show Deployment ad scaling ad-6cb57f76d from 0 to 1 at 22:13:21, pod ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 scheduled 22:13:21 and container ad created/started 22:13:23, then Deployment ad scaling ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0 at 22:13:24 and pod ad-554b849958-mbnxm being killed at 22:13:24; the same sequence occurred for payment (payment-9c8ffb665 scaled up 22:13:21, container started 22:13:24, payment-55766d76b9 scaled 1 to 0 and pod payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb killed 22:13:25).

Deployment otel-demo/ad is at revision 2 with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad and pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T22:13:21Z, and its container spec sets readinessProbe, livenessProbe and startupProbe all to null; Deployment otel-demo/payment likewise carries kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T22:13:21Z with readinessProbe/livenessProbe/startupProbe null and image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment.

The old and new ad ReplicaSets use the same image and the same environment (AD_PORT=8080, FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013, OTEL_* values): ad-554b849958 is revision 1, replicas 0, created 21:39:37; ad-6cb57f76d is revision 2, replicas 1, ready 1, created 22:13:21 (payment shows the same revision-1/revision-2 pattern with identical env).

Pod ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 has restartCount 0, container ad state running startedAt 2026-11-17T22:13:23Z, and a Ready condition with lastTransitionTime 2026-11-17T22:13:24Z; pod payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 is similarly Ready=True at 22:13:25Z with container startedAt 22:13:24Z and restartCount 0.

The ad container's first log line in the 22:16–22:18 query window is 'Ad service starting.' at 2026-11-17T22:17:48.827Z, with no earlier lines (the view reports 0 lines before the window start and 275 after its end); later log lines show it handling 'Targeted ad request received for [...]' and 'Non-targeted ad request received' entries between 22:22:17 and 22:22:47.

ad's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds server-span increase per 5 minutes was 223.3 (window ending 22:15), 155.6, 101.2, 41.0 (ending 22:18), then 0 for the windows ending 22:19 through 22:23, then 100.9 (22:24), 149.4, 147.5, 139.7 and 62.0; every returned series carried status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET and no ERROR series was returned for this span.

The frontend's own client series for grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds shows ERROR increases rising 13.3 (22:15) to 260 (22:19) and falling to 0 by 22:26, while its STATUS_CODE_UNSET increases fell to 0 for the windows ending 22:19–22:22 and resumed at 61.1 (22:23) and 143.3 (22:24).
The payment container logged pairs of 'Charge request received.' and 'Transaction complete.' continuously between 22:15:42 and 22:15:56, i.e. during the fault window.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config key demo.flagd.json currently sets adFailure defaultVariant 'on' (description 'Fail ad service') and paymentFailure defaultVariant '100%' (description 'Fail payment service charge requests n%'), with adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure at 'off'/0.

At the time of the Kubernetes query (22:31:11, after the error burst ended) all 21 otel-demo pods were Running and ready with restartCount 0, including ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 and payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84; this is the cluster's later state, not a statement about the incident interval.

Leading explanation: the frontend error burst was caused by the simultaneous rolling replacement of the single ad and payment pods at 22:13:21–22:13:25 (imperative restart recorded as kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T22:13:21Z); because Deployment ad declares no readiness or startup probe, the new ad pod was accepted as Ready at 22:13:24 and the old pod was killed at 22:13:24, but the ad process only logged 'Ad service starting.' at 22:17:48, so the ad ClusterIP had no listening backend and frontend GetAds calls failed with ECONNREFUSED, producing the GET /api/data 500s; the parallel payment restart explains the smaller checkout connection-refused errors to payment's ClusterIP.

Alternative candidate: the fault-injection settings currently held in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (adFailure='on', paymentFailure='100%') are what injected the failures on the ad and payment workloads that were restarted at 22:13:21; this remains unproven because I could not see when those values were set, and a fault-injection failure would not by itself explain transport-level ECONNREFUSED at the Service ClusterIPs.

The observed frontend AdService failures are transport-level, not application-level: the failing trace contains no ad service span, the client error is gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE with connect ECONNREFUSED to the ad ClusterIP 100.65.180.246:8080, ad's own GetAds server spans never returned an ERROR status (only STATUS_CODE_UNSET) and dropped to 0 counts while the errors ran, and the payment container logged successful 'Charge request received.'/'Transaction complete.' pairs during the same interval.

Add a readiness probe (gRPC/TCP on port 8080) and, preferably, a startup probe to the ad and payment container templates so a replacement pod is not added to the Service endpoints before its process is listening; ad currently has no readiness, liveness or startup probe.

Trace which operator, CI job or script issued the rollout restart recorded as kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T22:13:21Z on the ad and payment Deployments, and avoid restarting single-replica dependencies of the frontend during active load.

gaps: Who or what issued the rollout restart at 22:13:21Z (and why both ad and payment were restarted together) is not observable: only the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation timestamp exists, and the change_history integration is not available in this Run.

The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not loaded in the queried Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no rules), so the alert expression, the metric it uses and the meaning of the annotation value 'current: 2.5777777777777775' could not be verified.

kube-state-metrics series were queried with the documented selectors (kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready{namespace=otel-demo,deployment=~ad|payment|frontend}, name pattern kube_.*) and returned no data on this target, so pod readiness/endpoint history over the incident could not be measured; readiness transition times are available only as current pod conditions.
No log lines were returned for the frontend container (frontend-675fd7b5c5-h8sk5) in 22:10–22:22, so frontend-side error text is known only from spans.

The gRPC-js error text embeds the timestamp 2025-12-15T17:50:45.363Z for the last failed connect attempt, which does not match the incident date, so the exact moment of the last connection attempt cannot be verified from that string.

When the flagd-config values adFailure='on' and paymentFailure='100%' were written, and whether the ad and payment processes evaluate them, could not be determined; payment successfully completed charges during the window, which those settings do not explain.
The Kubernetes query for NetworkPolicy objects in otel-demo returned no objects, so a policy-based cause can be neither confirmed nor excluded from that query alone.

The reason the ad process took from container start at 22:13:23Z until 'Ad service starting.' at 22:17:48Z (about 4 minutes 25 seconds) is not visible in the available logs, and metric series for the ad JVM (kube_*/rpc_*/http_* names) returned no data.
next_steps: Review cluster audit logs / GitOps or CI history for the entity that patched the ad and payment Deployment pod templates at 2026-11-17T22:13:21Z (the restartedAt annotation), since change history is not integrated here.
Add and configure readiness/startup probes for ad and payment (and consider maxUnavailable/maxSurge settings for single-replica deployments) so endpoint removal waits for application readiness.

Confirm the flagd-config values actually reaching ad and payment (currently adFailure='on', paymentFailure='100%') and whether a deliberate fault-injection experiment was scheduled at 22:13; record the change time so it can be correlated with the incident.
Load or export the RequestErrorRate alert rule so its expression and threshold can be evaluated against the observed frontend error spans.

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics:
    dimensions:
    - default: otel-demo
      name: namespace
exporters:
  clickhouse:
    endpoint: http://clickhouse-clickhouse.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local:8123
    logs_table_name: otel_demo_logs
    password: ""
    traces_table_name: otel_demo_traces
    username: default
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch-master.opensearch.svc.cluster.local:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel-logs
    logs_index_time_format: yyyy-MM-dd
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector.opentelemetry-collectors.svc.cluster.local:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    endpoint: http://prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus.prometheus.svc.cluster.local:9090
    tls:
      insecure: true
  prometheus:
    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:8889
extensions:
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  resourcedetection:
    detectors:
    - env
    - system
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  nginx:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: http://image-provider:8081/status
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  postgresql:
    endpoint: postgresql:5432
    metrics:
      postgresql.blks_hit:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.blks_read:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.deadlocks:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_deleted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_fetched:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_inserted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_returned:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_updated:
        enabled: true
    password: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
    tls:
      insecure: true
    username: root
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
    username: valkey
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - debug
      - prometheus
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - nginx
      - otlp
      - postgresql
      - redis
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - pull:
          exporter:
            prometheus:
              host: 0.0.0.0
              port: 8888
